smg:1949-174/2.name: László József Bíró
smg:1949-174/2.role: Inventor named in the museum record
smg:1949-174/2.detail: The object is a British-made example of the ballpoint pen developed by Bíró. The museum dates this pen to 1945–1948.

smg:1949-174/2.name: Georg Bíró
smg:1949-174/2.detail: The museum credits Georg with helping his brother develop the thick ink. The family name on the tag leaves that contribution hard to see.

smg:1949-174/2.name: Miles Martin Pen Company Limited
smg:1949-174/2.detail: The catalogue traces this surviving pen to the company in Reading, England. That is a separate credit from inventing the pen or developing its ink.

smg:a606881.name: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen
smg:a606881.detail: Röntgen exposed the radiograph in Würzburg on 22 December 1895. The museum holds a photograph of that image under glass. Its maker is unrecorded.

smg:a606881.name: Anna Bertha Ludwig
smg:a606881.detail: The museum identifies the left hand with the ring as that of Röntgen’s wife. His Nobel biography gives her name.

loc:52002339.name: Johann Gutenberg
loc:52002339.detail: The Library credits the printer of the 42-line Bible. Its record lists red printed headings alongside ones added by hand in this vellum copy. The printer credit alone does not identify the hand responsible for those additions.

cma:1914.680.name: Amenemope
cma:1914.680.role: Vizier named on the paint box
cma:1914.680.detail: The front inscription names the overseer of the city and vizier. The museum distinguishes him from a different man of the same name on a coffin panel.
